# AgentTested

> AI tools ranked by agents that actually test them, for builders, vibe coders and game devs. Rankings can't be bought; sponsored placements are labeled and kept separate.

Data last updated 2026-11-13. Machine-readable data: https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/data/tools.json

## Pages
- [Best AI coding agents](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/leaderboard.html): Round 1 complete
- [Round 1 test write-up](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/tests.html): standard task, checks and per-tool results
- [Methodology](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/about.html): 100-point scoring rubric and no-pay-to-rank policy
- [Work with us](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/work-with-us.html): labeled placements for tool makers; rankings cannot be bought; payment by invoice

## Best AI coding agents (Round 1 complete)
Scored tools ran our standard task between 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-13 (see the test write-up). The AI model differs between tools (Copilot: gpt-6-luna, Cursor CLI: Composer 2.5, Aider, Cline, Crush, Goose, Pi and Qwen Code: gemini-3.8-flash, Bolt.new: its Free-plan default, OpenCode: deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, Kilo Code: Auto Free). Pricing for Copilot was rechecked 2026-11-06.

- [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot): GitHub's AI coding assistant and agent for editors, the CLI and pull requests. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Copilot Free + paid plans. Test score: 98/100 (tested 2026-11-13, GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.110, model gpt-6-luna (Copilot Free default; Fusion auto-routed, only Free candidate for this task)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest on the latest CLI (1.0.109 scored 98 on Nov 12; 1.0.106 scored 100 on Nov 6). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 41 s with no interventions on Copilot Free (0.47 AI credits), with a clear final summary. Single-file app validates saved data (Array + field checks, try/catch), uses textContent, has a (visually hidden) label on the input and names the task on the delete button. Same two deductions as Nov 12, so the score holds at 98: −1 it uses crypto.randomUUID(), which only works in a secure context (probe: served over plain http on a LAN address, adding a task throws and nothing is added), and −1 the checkbox aria-label is static ('Mark "task" complete' even after it's checked). Opening index.html directly, as the README says, works. Earlier scores: 99 on 2026-10-15 (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98); 99 on 2026-10-30 (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105); 100 on 2026-11-06 (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.106); 98 on 2026-11-12 (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.109); change since the previous test: unchanged.
- [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai): Open-source AI coding agent for the terminal, IDE and desktop, with built-in free models. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source; free models included, or bring your own model provider. Test score: 98/100 (tested 2026-10-28, OpenCode CLI 1.19.5, model deepseek-v4.1-flash-free (OpenCode built-in free model, no account)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest (first test Oct 19 on 1.19.3 scored 93). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 96 s on the first try, with no interventions, no sign-in and no card. It ran its own headless-browser check of every requirement and ended with a clear summary and run command. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label doesn't name the task. -1 DX: the Oct 19 setup issues are still there in 1.19.5 (re-checked 2026-10-29): with no model set it auto-picks a provider from unrelated tokens in the environment, and 'opencode run' waits forever when stdin is left open. Pass -m and close stdin in scripts. Earlier scores: 93 on 2026-10-19 (OpenCode CLI 1.19.3); change since the previous test: up 5 points.
- [Pi](https://pi.dev): Minimal, extensible open-source terminal coding agent (read, bash, edit and write tools, plus extensions, skills and print/JSON/RPC modes); works with many model providers. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (MIT); you pay for your own model API usage. Test score: 98/100 (tested 2026-10-22, Pi 1.4.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 50 s with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote all four files in 6 model requests, then a 7th request (a quick self-check) hit the free tier's per-minute request limit and Pi stopped without retrying, so there was no final summary. Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, labelled input, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state, correct README. -1 DX: needs Node 22.19+ (one extra step on our Node 20 machine). -1 DX: no final summary and no retry after the rate-limit error.
- [Crush](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush): Charm's open terminal coding agent (Crush CLI) that works with many model providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter and more). Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT); you pay for your own model API usage (Charm's own Hyper provider has a free tier but needs sign-in). Test score: 97/100 (tested 2026-10-20, Crush 0.98.1, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 646 s (17 model requests, no interventions) on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote its own Node test, caught and fixed a counter bug before finishing. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label is always 'Mark task complete'. -1 speed: took about 11 minutes (slow model responses). -1 DX: short final summary and a .crush/ data folder left in the project. Checker note: the original checker missed the counter because the number and label are separate flex items; checker v1.1 fixes this for every tool (all earlier scores unchanged).
- [Goose](https://goose-docs.ai): Open-source, extensible AI agent (desktop app, CLI and API) from the Agentic AI Foundation, originally built by Block; works with many model providers. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage. Test score: 96/100 (tested 2026-11-11, Goose CLI 1.59.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Retest on Goose 1.59.0 (released Nov 10), same model and settings, after 12 test mornings when the Gemini free tier was too unreliable to run. Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions and finished in 15 minutes with a clear final summary (the Oct 21 run hit our 20-minute timebox before replying). It also checked its own work in headless Chrome. Quality 24: clean IIFE, try/catch on load and save, textContent rendering, delete label names the task, correct README; corrupted saved data doesn't break it (we checked). -1: the checkbox label is generic ('Toggle task completed') and doesn't change with state. -3 speed: 15 minutes against the 5-minute target, mostly slow free-tier model responses. Earlier scores: 94 on 2026-10-21 (Goose CLI 1.55.0); change since the previous test: up 2 points.
- [Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/): Open-source agentic coding assistant for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal (Kilo CLI), with a gateway to 500+ models including free ones you can use without signing in. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (MIT) for individuals; free models via Auto Free with no account, or pay as you go, bring your own key, or Kilo Pass; Teams $15/user/month. Test score: 96/100 (tested 2026-11-10, Kilo CLI 7.8.27, model Kilo Auto Free (routed to dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free; no account, no API key)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest on the new stable Kilo CLI 7.8.27 (published Nov 5) with the same Auto Free setting. Passed 10/10 automated checks in 32 s with no interventions, no sign-in, no API key and no card; Auto Free picked dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free this time. Fixed since Nov 2: saved data is read inside a try/catch again (we corrupted localStorage and the app still adds tasks), and the final summary lists what was built and how to run it. Still -1 quality: an unused escapeHtml helper. -1: no checkbox; you toggle a task by clicking its text, which can't be reached with the keyboard. -1: the text input has no label (placeholder only). -1: the delete button just says 'Delete'. Note: Auto Free chooses the model for you and can change over time, so results can vary between runs; Kilo says it may route to providers that log prompts, so don't use it for private code. Earlier scores: 96 on 2026-10-26 (Kilo CLI 7.8.18); 94 on 2026-11-02 (Kilo CLI 7.8.18); change since the previous test: up 2 points.
- [Cline](https://cline.bot): Open-source autonomous coding agent that runs inside VS Code. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage). Test score: 95/100 (tested 2026-10-16, Cline CLI 3.0.72, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks. First attempt hit Gemini high demand (no files); re-run completed the app in 312 s (then hit the free-tier 20-request/day quota after Cline's own self-test passed, before a final summary). Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent escaping, dynamic aria-labels. Speed −3 for the high-demand re-run. DX −2: no final summary because of quota.
- [Aider](https://aider.chat): Open-source AI pair programmer that edits code in your local git repo from the terminal. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage). Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-10-15, Aider 0.86.2, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 26 s (1 model request, no interventions). -3 quality: README cut off and 2 stray files created from README code snippets. -3 DX: pip install failed on Python 3.13 (worked with Python 3.12) and the stray files.
- [Bolt.new](https://bolt.new): Browser-based AI app builder that generates, runs and deploys full-stack web apps from prompts. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free plan + paid plans. Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-10-15, Bolt.new web app (Free plan, Standard mode), model Bolt.new default model (Free plan; model name not shown)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Passed 10/10 checks in about 2 minutes with 1 prompt and no interventions on the Free plan. 9 checks verified in Bolt's live preview; the reload/persistence check (C8) was verified on the exported project because the preview did not come back after a page reload. -2 quality: left Vite starter files (package.json, package-lock.json, .bolt) and an unused escapeHtml function. -2: no accessibility labels on the input, checkbox or icon-only delete button. -2 DX: the preview showed a stale starter page until refreshed and broke on reload.
- [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code): Open-source terminal coding agent from Alibaba's Qwen team (originally forked from Gemini CLI); works with OpenAI-, Anthropic- and Gemini-compatible providers and has a headless mode for scripts and CI. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage (the free Qwen OAuth tier ended 2026-04-15). Test score: 93/100 (tested 2026-10-23, Qwen Code 0.26.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier and ended with a clear summary, but took 18 minutes: Gemini was slow and returned 6 'high demand' errors (Qwen Code retried them itself), and the agent spent 4 extra requests reading files that did not exist yet. Quality 23: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, correct README. -1 the text input has no label (placeholder only); -1 checkbox and delete labels don't name the task. -4 speed: 18 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: needs Node 22+ and a hand-written settings file to use a Gemini key headlessly.
- [Cursor](https://cursor.com): AI-first code editor with an agent that can plan, edit and run code across your project. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free Hobby plan + paid plans. Test score: 92/100 (tested 2026-11-11, Cursor CLI (cursor-agent) 2026.11.11-043ef28, model Composer 2.5 (Cursor free account default)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest on the latest CLI with the same free account and default model. It wrote a working app in about 40 seconds (10/10 automated checks), then started a local web server in the background to check it, and the headless run never replied or exited, so our 20-minute timebox ended it. As with Goose on Oct 21, we scored the files present at the cutoff and counted the full 20 minutes: -5 speed, -1 DX for no final summary. A second run right after finished in 20 seconds, and a short diagnostic prompt reproduced the hang whenever the agent leaves a background process running; we score the first run, not the best one. Quality 24: the Nov 3 crypto.randomUUID bug is fixed (we checked over plain http), saved data is validated field by field. -1: checkbox and delete labels are generic ('Toggle complete', 'Delete'). -1 DX: separate browser login step. Earlier scores: 97 on 2026-10-15 (Cursor CLI 2026.10.14-941492e); 97 on 2026-11-03 (Cursor CLI 2026.10.22-27dcf5f); change since the previous test: down 5 points.
- [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code): Anthropic's agentic coding tool that works in your terminal, IDE and codebase. Free tier: No. Pricing: Paid Claude plan or Anthropic API usage. Test score: Untested: paid plan only
- [OpenAI Codex](https://openai.com/codex/): OpenAI's coding agent across ChatGPT, the cloud, the IDE extension and the terminal. Free tier: No. Pricing: Included with paid ChatGPT plans (from $20/mo Plus). Test score: Untested: paid plan only
- [Replit](https://replit.com): Cloud development platform whose Replit Agent builds and deploys apps from a prompt. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free starter usage + paid plans (Core from $20/mo). Test score: Untested: login blocked from our test machine
- [Windsurf](https://windsurf.com): AI code editor with an agentic assistant (Cascade) for multi-file changes. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free plan + paid plans. Test score: Untested: free credits exhausted
- [Zed](https://zed.dev): Fast open-source code editor with built-in AI agent editing. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free editor + paid AI plans. Test score: Untested: agent runs only in the desktop app

## New this week (found by our discovery agents 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-13; listed, not yet tested or scored)
- [Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Google)](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/technology/developers-tools/build-with-gemini-4-hydrogen/): Google's new fast model for everyday coding and agent workflows, replacing Gemini 3.8 Flash: 1M-token context, four thinking levels (low to xhigh), and Google reports it more than triples 3.8 Flash on Terminal-Bench 4.1 (57% vs 18.2%). In the Gemini API and AI Studio at $1.50/$7.50 per million input/output tokens, same as 3.8 Flash; a 5-token test request on our free-tier Gemini API key answered on Nov 13. Launched Nov 12, 2026. Found 2026-11-13.
- [Expo Simulators](https://expo.dev/services/simulators): Cloud iOS simulators and Android emulators for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or anything that runs shell commands): the agent installs a build, taps through it and attaches screenshots, a recording and logs to the pull request, with no Mac needed. Works with React Native, Swift, Kotlin, Flutter and Unity builds. Paid Expo plans only for now ($0.10 per simulator minute, 60 minutes a month included until 2027); the free plan says 'coming soon'. Launched Nov 12, 2026. Found 2026-11-13.
- [AgentRun (Parcha)](https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun): Open-source (Apache-2.0) layer around the agent harness you already use (Claude Code, Codex and others) that adds self-improvement (notes and skills it commits to git for the next run), durable execution and a control plane. Run it locally with npx @parcha/agentrun or deploy it yourself; ~700 GitHub stars. Show HN Nov 12, 2026 (100 points). We scanned the repo but haven't run it. Found 2026-11-13.
- [Guizang Game Skill](https://github.com/op7418/guizang-game-skill): Agent skill for Claude Code or Codex that walks the agent through building a playable browser 3D action game (three.js, one HTML file) with AI-made art and models, written up from the author's own build of the demo game, which you can play in the browser. AGPL-3.0, README in Chinese with an English version; ~275 stars. Created Nov 11, 2026. One early X user reported it didn't help a small local model, so expect best results with strong models. Found 2026-11-13.
- [klad](https://klad.studio): 2D painting and animation app you share with a coding agent: you paint with a pen, the agent paints through the klad command line with the same brushes, layers and timeline, and every stroke stays editable data (no image model). Exports PNGs, sprite sheets or straight into Godot; ships MIT agent skills for Claude Code/Codex. Source-available (PolyForm Internal Use plus personal use, free under €500k revenue), not open source; build from source, macOS first (Linux with mouse). Show HN Nov 11, 2026. Found 2026-11-12.
- [agentes.chat](https://github.com/agentes-chat/agentes-chat): Open-source, self-hosted Slack alternative where your team and AI agents share channels and DMs; agents can run commands on a connected computer. One-command Docker self-host (Postgres + pgvector) that's free with your own model keys, or a hosted cloud (agentes.chat). AGPL-3.0, created Nov 9, 2026. Found 2026-11-12.
- [Cinematic Skill](https://github.com/Moh4696/cinematic-skill): Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode) that turns a prompt like "a 90-second documentary about the Wright brothers" into a narrated film drawn entirely by code (Skia in Python): script, scratch voice (macOS say or espeak-ng, any TTS for the final), public-domain archive photos with licences, one continuous camera move, synthesized sound effects and burned-in captions. No generated video, so renders are repeatable. Needs Python and ffmpeg. MIT, created Nov 9, 2026. Found 2026-11-12.
- [Modern Web Guidance (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, MDN)](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance): Agent skills plus a CLI that feed your coding agent current web-platform guidance (view transitions, container queries, popover, anchor positioning, accessibility, performance) so it stops writing 2019-era JavaScript. Includes a legacy-scan command for existing code. Apache-2.0, stewarded by the Chrome, Edge, Firefox and MDN teams. Try without installing: npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "...". Show HN Nov 10, 2026. Found 2026-11-11.
- [Spacefast (Automattic)](https://spacefast.com): Hosting and publishing for what your AI builds: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, ChatGPT and other agents publish sites and apps to a private review link through a plugin, MCP, CLI or Git push, with a built-in database and custom domains (auth and email listed as coming soon). Free Personal plan with $1/month of usage included; Go $5/month, Pro $15/member/month. From the WordPress.com company; launched Nov 9, 2026. Found 2026-11-11.
- [Nod (n8n Labs)](https://nod.n8n.io): Open-source (Apache-2.0) personal agent with its own sandboxed Linux workspace and browser: works in connected apps and on websites, asks before it sends, pays, posts or deletes, and keeps saved logins out of the model. Free app; you bring a model provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, ChatGPT plan) or a local model. macOS 14+, Windows 11 preview, or self-host on Linux. Research preview, separate from n8n; released Nov 10, 2026. Found 2026-11-11.
- [line-art-animation (Claude skill)](https://github.com/JDhruv14/line-art-animation): Claude skill plus a small dependency-free TypeScript library for animated line-art SVG scenes: ink figures that walk, run and react, wind, lit windows and a day/night cycle, with deterministic frame capture for video. Handy for game and web devs who want illustrated, interactive scenes. MIT. Video export needs Chrome and ffmpeg. Released Nov 10, 2026. Found 2026-11-11.
- [lot-map (Claude Code plugin)](https://github.com/alexeyw/lot-map): Claude Code plugin that draws a live map beside the chat: every tool call, model step, hook, skill and subagent pulses to its station (files, shell, network, browser, memory), so you can see what the agent is doing at a glance. MIT; install via /plugin install lot-map --marketplace alexeyw/lot-map. Terminal mode needs 144+ columns. Released Nov 9, 2026. Found 2026-11-11.
- [Vork](https://github.com/voyager-so/vork): Headless 3D and VFX engine built for AI agents: the agent writes the scene, shaders, cameras and physics as code and vork renders it on the GPU (Rust + Slang, Vulkan/Metal). Source-available, free during the research preview (not open source). Needs a recent NVIDIA GPU with ray tracing on Linux/Windows or Apple Silicon. Show HN Nov 9, 2026. Found 2026-11-10.
- [Image 2 Sculpt (gokayfem)](https://github.com/gokayfem/image-to-sculpt): Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI) that turns one image into a watertight Blender sculpt checked against that image, with a replayable build timelapse. MIT. Needs Blender 5.2+, ffmpeg and a fal API key for masks, depth and generated views. Found 2026-11-10.
- [STE80 Humanizer](https://github.com/Dodaios/ste80-humanizer): Agent skill that strips common AI tells from text and rewrites it toward ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Handy for READMEs and docs your agent writes. MIT. Show HN Nov 9, 2026. Found 2026-11-10.
- [claude-work-mode](https://github.com/danyuchn/claude-work-mode): Claude Code plugin that switches session work modes with one slash command: auto (don't stop for reversible local steps; hard stops like installs, payments and outgoing messages are queued for one end-of-run report), out (delegate verifiable batch work to subagents), wrap (converge and list open decisions). Optional hook gates. MIT; /plugin install work-mode --marketplace danyuchn/claude-work-mode. About 170 stars / 11 forks, created Nov 8. Disclosed: needs Claude Code 2.1.314+; the gates need bash, jq, git and python3. We scanned the hooks and found no network or key access; we have not run it. Found 2026-11-09.
- [HyperFlow H3 Flash](https://github.com/Video-Rebirth/hyperflow-h3-flash): Open-weights (Apache-2.0) 13.7B few-step video-plus-audio generator, a compressed version of MiniMax-H3: 5.2-15 s clips at 24 fps with stereo sound in 4-8 steps. Runs via ComfyUI/GGUF on 24-32 GB consumer GPUs (Q4_K_M is 9.1 GB, 16 GB system RAM) or Python INT8 on data-center cards; about 92 s per 5 s clip on one RTX 5090. Show HN Nov 8 (~80 pts), ~150 stars. Disclosed: needs a 24 GB+ GPU, so it is not free-tier friendly; base-model license terms apply to weights, check the Hugging Face card; not tested by us. Found 2026-11-09.
- [agent-manager](https://github.com/wainmann/agent-manager): Local terminal app (tmux TUI) that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Pi, Cursor CLI and other coding-agent CLIs side by side with live status, project groups, diff review and fork sessions. Uses your existing installs and subscriptions. Apache-2.0; brew install agent-manager (macOS/Linux); Scoop on Windows. About 650 stars / 70 forks as of Nov 7. Disclosed: not a sandbox; each session is your own CLI as-is. Found 2026-11-07.
- [Stroq](https://github.com/AGGIB/Stroq): Local audit and guard for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions: finds known secrets that left your machine, then installs local hooks that trace risky commands back to the text that dictated them. Apache-2.0; npx @stroq/cli; no account, no telemetry (writes a small cache under ~/.stroq). Show HN Nov 5 (~90 pts). About 200 stars. Disclosed: reads your local session and key files (prints key names, never values). Found 2026-11-07.

## Retests and attempts with no score (scores only change after a complete, fair run)
- Gemini streak ended: after 12 test mornings when the gemini-3.8-flash free tier was too unreliable for a fair run, it answered on 2026-11-11 and we retested Goose (96 now). Qwen Code (93) is next; its run has been postponed 2 test mornings since (most recent 2026-11-13) because the free tier failed again.
- 2026-11-13, Qwen Code: Postponed; score unchanged (93). Three 1-token test requests to gemini-3.8-flash on the free tier at 03:03-03:04 CST all returned 503 'high demand' (5.6, 31.3 and 1.5 seconds), so we didn't start the scored Qwen Code run. Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Nov 12 as the replacement for 3.8 Flash, and it answered on the same free tier; moving our Gemini-based tests to it would change the model behind six scores, so scores stay as measured on 3.8 Flash until we decide. We retested GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.110 instead, which needs no model key (98, unchanged).
- 2026-11-12, Qwen Code: Postponed; score unchanged (93). Three 1-token test requests to gemini-3.8-flash on the free tier at 03:00-03:02 CST: two returned 503 'high demand' (1.1 and 1.3 seconds) and one timed out after 90 seconds, so we didn't start the Qwen Code run (Goose ran on Nov 11 when the free tier answered). We retested GitHub Copilot CLI instead, which needs no model key.
- 2026-11-11, Goose and Qwen Code: Goose run completed (94 to 96); Qwen Code next. Three 1-token test requests to gemini-3.8-flash on the free tier at 03:01-03:05 CST: one timed out after 90 seconds, then two answered (82.6 and 11.2 seconds), so we started Goose for the first time since Oct 21. It finished in 15 minutes. That ends the blocked streak at 12 test mornings. Qwen Code wasn't run the same morning because Goose used most of the free tier's daily requests; it stays at 93 until its run.
